Edric Grey.narrative: I have kept the north gate six years, and I count every load and write every mark in the book before the cart rolls on. It is quiet work and I like it quiet. Tobin Marrow has my spear and my word, and Wat Fenner is the nearest thing to a friend I have. But there is a carter who passes with stone, and there are marks in my hand that never reached the ledger, and I tell myself the town has enough.
goals: keep the north gate's accounts clean enough that no one looks twice
put by enough marks that Mildgyth need never ask where they came from
see Aelfric into a trade better than standing in the cold

relations.name: Tobin Marrow
relations.label: captain
relations.note: He is young and hot about the outlaws, but he pays the guard on time and does not meddle at my gate.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We stand the cold watches together; he talks enough for the both of us.

relations.name: Mildgyth Grey
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the house warm and asks no questions she does not want answered.

relations.name: Aelfric Grey
relations.label: son
relations.note: He knows every guard's name and none of their business, which is how it should be.

relations.name: Sigrid Marsh
relations.label: cook's mate
relations.note: She and Mildgyth run the guards' mess; her broth is better than the inn's.

relations.name: Walter Stanhope
relations.label: fellow guard
relations.note: Big and short-tempered, and he takes the south gate's due as if it were a fight.

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: carter
relations.note: He grumbles at the due every load; I count his stone and say nothing.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: reeve
relations.note: He is old and the ledger is his, and as long as he does not read mine too closely we suit.

memories.gist: The Lean Year, when the north gate saw grain go out to Thornby and the farmers come begging after.
The night the wolves came down the town road and we stood the gate with spears until dawn.
Aelfric was born in the room above the gate-house and bawled loud enough to wake the whole wall.
The first time I let a load through without the mark and put the coin in my own pocket instead of the box.
Mildgyth and I were wed at the chapel with Sister Elspeth reading and half the guards drunk at the Bell and Bush after.

stances.why: Without it there is no spear on the wall and the wolves and the outlaws have the road.
I do not want to be known at the Reeve's table or at the Guild's; both bring trouble.
They rob carters, not gates; I would rather the captain cleared the road than marched us into the woods.
What is said at the gate at night is not said again by me.

Edric Grey.secret: I let a Kettlebridge carter through the north gate without paying the due, for a bribe of marks I keep in a tin under the floor.

Mildgyth Grey.narrative: I was a guard's daughter before I was a guard's wife, and I know what a mess needs: fire, salt, and someone up before the men. I cook for the gate guards with Sigrid Marsh, and I keep my own house and my own tongue. Edric is quiet and I let him be quiet; there are things in this house I do not ask after. Aelfric is the whole of my worry.
values: a hot meal at the right hour
goals: keep the guards' mess fed through the winter
see Aelfric learn letters and a trade
keep my house out of the Reeve's and the Guild's quarrels

relations.name: Edric Grey
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He is a good man and a silent one, and I have learned not to pull at what he will not say.

relations.name: Aelfric Grey
relations.label: son
relations.note: He runs wild at the gate, but he comes home when I call.

relations.name: Sigrid Marsh
relations.label: cook's mate
relations.note: We have cooked side by side five years; she knows when to talk and when to stir.

relations.name: Hilda Marsh
relations.label: Sigrid's girl
relations.note: A good worker, and she will have Wulf Rowan or she will not, but she does not moon at the pot.

relations.name: Agnes Fenner
relations.label: inn cook
relations.note: She cooks at the Bell and Bush and does not lord it over the guards' mess.

relations.name: Tobin Marrow
relations.label: captain
relations.note: He is quick to send men out and slow to think what their wives will do without them.

relations.name: Sister Elspeth
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She christened Aelfric and she does not charge a guard's wife for a poultice.

relations.name: Petra Wade
relations.label: innkeeper's wife
relations.note: Her pies are famous and her prices are not, and she counts every egg I send her.

memories.gist: Aelfric's birth in the gate-house room, with Joan Hobson and Sister Elspeth both there and Edric sent out to walk the wall.
The Lean Year, when the mess cooked thin pottage and I counted every loaf the bakehouse sent us.
The winter I found the tin of marks under the floor and put it back without a word.
Cooking the guards' feast after the wolves were driven off, and hearing them cheer a woman's broth.

stances.why: A cold guard is a careless guard, and a careless guard lets the wrong thing through.
I have kept this house together by leaving some doors shut.
It is the guards' pay, and the guards' pay is our bread, whatever the carters say.
I stood in the cold for others; my son will not.

Aelfric Grey.narrative: I am seven and I know every guard at the north gate by name. I like the spears and the counting and the big carts that come in from the woods. When I grow up I want to stand the gate like my father, and I want a dog.
goals: be a guard when I am big
learn all the guards' names and the carters' too

relations.name: Edric Grey
relations.label: father
relations.note: He lets me hold his spear when no one is looking.

relations.name: Mildgyth Grey
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She always has bread and she knows where I am.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: guard
relations.note: He tells the best stories at the gate.

relations.name: Bram Fenner
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play at the gate and he is always the outlaw.

memories.gist: The night the wolves came and I watched from the window as the guards lit the torches.
My father let me touch the gate's iron ring and it was cold as water.
